SMTO-EXE-0171 — Spreadsheet results may be out of date

GUID: f4839356-2273-54c8-a24a-710040068e40
Slug: office-formula-not-calculated
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: office

What happened

  • SMTO shows the result that was last saved for a formula, but it never recalculates formulas itself, so the number may be old. Nothing in the file was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the spreadsheet in Excel, LibreOffice Calc or another spreadsheet app you trust. Those apps recalculate formulas when they open or save the file.
  2. Save the file in that app so the updated results are stored. SMTO reads the results saved in the file, so they must be saved first.
  3. Ask SMTO to read the spreadsheet again. SMTO will then see the freshly calculated values.

What success looks like

  • The values SMTO reports match what your spreadsheet app shows.

If it still fails

  • SMTO is designed never to run formulas, so there's no setting to change. If the values still look wrong after saving, send the copied error details and the file name to the person who manages SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • office.formula_not_calculated is a retained identity with no current failure branch; SMTO's Excel reads return formula text and the stored cached value separately and never calculate formulas, so cached values may be stale.

What this means

  • The retained formula-not-calculated identity has no direct current failure branch; Excel reads distinguish formula text from cached values and never calculate formulas. Office workers treat document content as untrusted data and never execute macros or formulas. Publication creates a separate output under existing File policy; retain revision and effect facts before any new write.

Why this can happen

  • The retained formula-not-calculated identity has no direct current failure branch; Excel reads distinguish formula text from cached values and never calculate formulas.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect formula and cached-value fields separately and any projection warning; do not treat an absent/stale cache as a newly calculated result.

How to fix it

  • Treat cached values as possibly stale (calculation_state=external_recalc_required after edits). SMTO has no calculation engine; recalculate and save the workbook in a trusted spreadsheet application, then re-read it.
  • Treat cached values as possibly stale. SMTO does not calculate formulas; use a trusted spreadsheet application separately.

Retry and execution caution

  • Treat cached values as possibly stale. SMTO does not calculate formulas; use a trusted spreadsheet application separately.

How to verify the fix

  • The output identifies formula text and cached data honestly, with any required recalculation performed in a separate trusted application.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay uncertain writes or execute embedded document content.

Technical notes

  • Office workers treat document content as untrusted data and never execute macros or formulas. Publication creates a separate output under existing File policy; retain revision and effect facts before any new write.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
